players.name: Ja'Kobi Lane
players.outlook: Lane was selected by the Ravens in the third round of April's draft. Lane is a tall, perimeter receiver with the biggest hands in this rookie class. He produced solid 43-525-12 and 49-745-4 receiving lines during his final two seasons at USC. Lane was rarely used in the intermediate area and struggled to produce after the catch (career 3.7 RAC is second worst in this class), but he has the frame and skill set to allow him plenty of pro potential. He'll battle the likes of Devontez Walker and fellow rookie Elijah Surratt for work behind Zay Flowers and Rashod Bateman in Baltimore's low-volume p

players.name: Greg Dulcich
players.outlook: Dulcich is back on the fantasy radar as the top tight end on the Miami depth chart. The 2022 third-round pick for the Denver Broncos made some noise as a rookie with a 33-411-2 receiving line in 10 games, but he went on to total 16 targets during the 2023 and 2024 seasons before landing in Miami last season. Dulcich didn't see his first target until Week 9 but went on to post a 26-335-1 receiving line the rest of the way. He wasn't a regular fantasy option (one top-15 week among TEs), but he certainly has a path to a substantial target share in 2026 with minimal competition at tight end and wi

players.name: Kaelon Black
players.outlook: Black was selected by the 49ers in the third round of April's draft. It was a bit of a surprise selection after Black failed to clear 190 touches in four collegiate seasons prior to not landing an invite to the scouting combine. He did clear 1,000 rushing yards at Indiana in 2025, but remained a nonfactor as a receiver, totaling exactly four receptions in each of his two seasons with the Hoosiers. Black will open his career in a battle with Jordan James for No. 2 duties behind Christian McCaffrey. He'll be worth an add if the 30-year-old McCaffrey misses time, but a lack of third-down ability

players.name: Caleb Douglas
players.outlook: Douglas was selected by the Dolphins in the third round of April's draft. Douglas is a tall, perimeter receiver with big hands and long arms who, after not seeing much work during two seasons at Florida, exploded for 60-877-6 and 54-846-7 receiving lines at Texas Tech over the last two seasons. His overall efficiency was underwhelming, including six drops and a shaky 1.81 YPRR in 2025. He impressed with a 4.39 40-yard dash at 206 pounds (111 speed score) at the combine. Douglas has a path to a large offensive role as a rookie (Malik Washington, Jalen Tolbert and fellow rookie Chris Bell are hi

players.name: Kaytron Allen
players.outlook: Allen was selected by the Commanders in the sixth round of April's draft. Allen has a good size and a solid efficiency profile, having ranked seventh in this rookie class in YAC (3.35) and 10th in forced missed tackle rate (4.5) during his four seasons at Penn State. Though he out-carried fellow draft prospect Nicholas Singleton in all four seasons at PSU, Allen was less involved as a receiver (career 70-490-4 line, including a weak 5.1 YPT) and doesn't figure to get much run as a receiver in the pros. Allen is a long shot as a sixth-rounder, but he's a name to monitor considering the state of

players.name: Cade Otton
players.outlook: Otton re-signed with Tampa Bay after spending his first four NFL seasons with the team. Since entering the league in 2022, Otton ranks first among all tight ends in snaps (3,530) and second in routes (1,838). That simply hasn't translated to much target volume (he is yet to clear 86 in a season) or goal-line work (11 TDs and 19 end zone targets in 63 games). In fact, Otton was the only player with 75-plus targets who didn't score multiple touchdowns last season. The 27-year-old has finished 25th or lower in fantasy PPG in three of four seasons and is a poor bet for his first top-10 finish in 2

players.name: Germie Bernard
players.outlook: Bernard was selected by the Steelers in the second round of April's draft. Bernard is a solid, reliable receiver with good size who can align all over the formation (55% slot in 53 collegiate games). Despite playing at three schools in four years, Bernard's production increased each season, including a strong 64-862-7 receiving line (plus 18-101-2 rushing) in 2025. He dropped only four of 240 career targets. Bernard is likely to open his career third in line at receiver behind Michael Pittman Jr. and DK Metcalf. That will create a tough path to consistent rookie-season usage and production, so

players.name: Zachariah Branch
players.outlook: Branch was selected by the Falcons in the third round of April's draft. Branch is a tiny slot receiver who posted an extremely low 5.2 aDOT during 37 collegiate games. That limited his efficiency numbers a bit, though he caught 71% of his targets and was terrific after the catch (7.9 RAC). Branch has the look of a versatile (perhaps gadget) player who will help as a rusher, slot receiver and returner. That role makes him a longshot for consistent fantasy output, but he does have a path to No. 2 receiver duties behind Drake London with the likes of Olamide Zaccheaus and Jahan Dotson his primary

players.name: Steelers D/ST
players.outlook: The No. 1 D/ST selected on average last season, the Steelers finished a disappointing 14th in fantasy points and scored fewer than five points in 8-of-17 games. They've since overhauled their coaching staff, with Mike McCarthy replacing Mike Tomlin, and Patrick Graham as defensive coordinator, the same role he held with the Raiders from 2022-25. The offseason additions of S Jaquan Brisker and CB Jamel Dean should bolster this unit, and it benefits greatly from one of the softest September and October schedules in the league. Get this D/ST early, but be prepared to seek a replacement after that

players.name: Jaylen Wright
players.outlook: Wright will once again compete with second-year Ollie Gordon II for backup reps behind feature back De'Von Achane. Wright has barely cleared 70 touches during each of his first two NFL seasons, but he has shined at times, including a 24-107-1 rushing line in Week 14 last season. The 2024 fourth-round pick has been effective as a rusher, but hasn't been involved in the passing game (15 targets in 25 games). The 23-year-old would be worth adding only in the event of an Achane injury and even then, it's possible he would split (or be on the short end of a committee) with Gordon in a rebuilding of

players.name: Seahawks D/ST
players.outlook: The defending Super Bowl champions, who benefited greatly from what was the league's top-scoring fantasy defense, draw one of the toughest overall schedules as a ?reward.? Only the Cardinals (Weeks 2 and 9), Raiders (Week 10) and Giants (Week 14) appear to be clear plus matchups, and the team must also deal with the offseason losses of S Coby Bryant, edge rusher Boye Mafe and CB Riq Woolen. Mike Macdonald might extract maximum effort from his defenses, but some regression should be expected with this unit.

players.name: Antonio Williams
players.outlook: Williams was selected by the Commanders in the third round of April's draft. He is an undersized slot receiver (75% slot in his collegiate career) who soaked up 208 catches (fourth most in this rookie class) during his four seasons (43 games) at Clemson. He was primarily a short-range option (8.0 aDOT), but he caught a healthy 75% of his targets and added value as a rusher (career 25-187-2 rushing), punt returner and even as a passer (143 yards and two TDs on four attempts). Williams is in an all-out battle with the likes of Van Jefferson, Dyami Brown, Jaylin Lane and Treylon Burks for the No.

players.name: Rams D/ST
players.outlook: This already highly regarded defense only got stronger in June with the acquisition of two-time Defensive Player of the Year (2023, 2025) Myles Garrett. He wasn't their only addition, as CBs Trent McDuffie and Jaylen Watson were brought in from the Chiefs. Expect another productive season from this unit, though it does face one of the tougher early-season schedules, with the 49ers (Week 1), Broncos (3), Eagles (4) and Bills (5) among their first five opponents. The Rams' second-half schedule is one of the easiest, meaning they might be a better in-season trade target than a draft-day pickup.

players.name: Chris Bell
players.outlook: Bell was selected by the Dolphins in the third round of April's draft. The heaviest receiver in this rookie class at 222 pounds, Bell is a perimeter, possession target who increased his production in each of his four seasons at Louisville. That includes a 72-917-6 receiving line in 11 games last season, though he did tear his ACL in December. The injury could lead to a slow start to his NFL career, but considering he's joining a Miami offense devoid of playmakers, he also has a path to pacing the team in targets as a rookie. Bell could find his way to fantasy relevance if healthy and if Malik

players.name: Ravens D/ST
players.outlook: No team has as soft a schedule on the defensive side of things than do the Ravens; only the Cowboys (Week 3), Bengals (7 and 17) and Bills (8) stand out as particularly challenging matchups. That's a good thing, considering this unit finished a disappointing 21st in scoring last season. The Ravens still have stars on the defensive side, and the change in head coach to Jesse Minter and defensive coordinator to Anthony Weaver should fuel a rebound to some degree.

players.name: Malachi Fields
players.outlook: Fields was selected by the Giants in the third round of April's draft. One of the biggest and strongest receivers in this rookie class, Fields figures to work as a perimeter, vertical target in the pros (career 13.3 aDOT during 49 collegiate games). Fields, who dropped just seven passes in college, handled a target share of, at least, 20% and air yard share of, at least, 30% during each of his final three collegiate seasons (two at Virginia, one at Notre Dame). Fields will battle Darnell Mooney and Darius Slayton for New York's No. 2 receiver gig behind Malik Nabers. The rookie is no more than

players.name: Eagles D/ST
players.outlook: Though the 2025 Eagles took a step backwards from the defensive stalwart that won Super Bowl LIX, their D/ST scored only 12 fewer total fantasy points and finished eighth at the position in scoring. Coordinator Vic Fangio typically extracts the most from his defenses, but the departures of S Reed Blankenship, LB Nakobe Dean, DE Brandon Graham and LB Jaelen Phillips heighten the challenge -- though the additions of LB Jonathan Greenard and CB Riq Woolen at least soften the blow. At least the team starts off with some soft matchups (WSH, Week 1; @TEN, Week 2), but be prepared to swap quickly if

players.name: Justice Hill
players.outlook: Hill heads into his seventh NFL season positioned for a larger role following the offseason departure of Keaton Mitchell. Derrick Henry remains the team's lead rusher, but he plays only about half of the snaps, leaving plenty of opportunity for Hill, particularly in passing situations. We've seen Hill in that role recently, including a 2024 campaign in which he posted a 42-383-3 receiving line on 55 targets (11th most among backs). Of course, Hill isn't trusted with much rushing work (his career high in carries is 84), which is why he has never had a top-35 fantasy campaign in his career. The

players.name: George Holani
players.outlook: Holani is on the 2026 fantasy radar with Kenneth Walker III no longer on the Seattle roster and Zach Charbonnet (ACL) in doubt for the early portion of the season. Holani will compete with rookie Jadrian Price, Emanuel Wilson and Kenny McIntosh for touches while Charbonnet is sidelined. The 2024 UDFA has 25 carries and three targets to his name through two NFL seasons. Price figures to get the first shot at lead back duties and, even if forced into a few starts in Seattle's run-friendly offense, Holani would be working in a committee and no more than a deep league flex.

players.name: Keon Coleman
players.outlook: So far, so bust for Coleman, who has struggled to make an impact after being selected 33rd overall in the 2024 draft. After flashing in a situational deep-threat role as a rookie (15.0 aDOT), Coleman saw more high percentage looks in 2025 (11.2 aDOT). That led to a much better catch rate (from 51% to 66%), but a big dip in yardage (19.2 YPR to 10.9). Coleman has yet to emerge as a reliable, full-time starter and was even a healthy scratch at times last season. Perhaps the 23-year-old will make a Year 3 leap with Joe Brady now running the show, but he'll have his hands full overtaking DJ Moore

players.name: Browns D/ST
players.outlook: The June trade of Myles Garrett quashed much of the enthusiasm surrounding the Browns' D/ST, though the team still has a trio of strong front-line defenders in Mason Graham, Jared Verse (the big return in the Garrett deal) and Carson Schwesinger and finished fourth at the position in fantasy points in 2025. Don't underestimate this unit, which has one of the softer early-season schedules, especially over the first five weeks (@JAX, @TB, CAR, PIT, @NYJ).

players.name: Evan Engram
players.outlook: Engram returns for his second season in Denver after an underwhelming debut campaign with the team. The veteran tight end was limited to a career-low 13% target share and finished 15th or lower among tight ends in routes, targets, catches and yardage, despite appearing in 16 games. Engram worked as a short-area target but still struggled to a poor 68% catch rate and was, as usual, a nonfactor near the goal line (one TD, two end zone targets). Engram hasn't cleared four touchdowns in a season since he scored six as a rookie in 2017. He finished 32nd among tight ends in fantasy PPG and isn't a g

players.name: Patriots D/ST
players.outlook: Zak Kuhr, elevated to the defensive coordinator position early last season, steered this D/ST to the sixth-most fantasy points and a Super Bowl LX berth. Now in the permanent role, he'll have a strengthened unit, with DE Dre'Mont Jones and S Kevin Byard brought on board, though it's fair to point out that the 2025 Patriots generated nearly one quarter of their fantasy points on defensive or special teams touchdowns. This is a team better used as a streaming than weekly defense, and bear in mind it has a tough-as-nails Super Bowl rematch in Seattle to begin the year.

players.name: Jack Bech
players.outlook: Bech is a candidate for a Year 2 leap after an underwhelming rookie campaign. The 2025 second-round pick was limited to 36% of Las Vegas' offensive snaps and cleared three targets in a game only twice. He failed to find the end zone while predominantly working as a short-range target. Bech will now compete with the likes of Tre Tucker, Jalen Nailor and Dont'e Thornton Jr. for a starting gig in a new-look offense led by coach Klint Kubiak and, at some point, No. 1 overall draft pick Fernando Mendoza. The 23-year-old is likely headed for a larger role in his second season and is worth a late-rou

players.name: Lions D/ST
players.outlook: Injuries have bred disappointing fantasy totals from the Lions' D/ST the past two seasons, as the team finished 12th and 17th despite what was a solid roster on paper. Fantasy managers should hope for better luck on that front, but at least the schedule will grant the Lions as good a chance to rebound as anything. They open with a home game against the Saints, have a trio of must-start matchups from Weeks 3-5 (NYJ, @CAR, @ARI) and one of the best second-half schedules.

players.name: Devaughn Vele
players.outlook: Vele is expected to open the season as New Orleans' No. 2 receiver behind Chris Olave until Jordyn Tyson returns from injury near midseason. Vele's first season with the Saints was marred with injuries. The 2024 seventh-round pick, who posted a 41-475-3 receiving line with Denver as a rookie, barely played throughout most of 2025 prior to taking on an every-down role during Weeks 10-15. In those five games (one of which he left hurt), he averaged 5.6 targets per game, but reached 12.0 fantasy points once (an 8-93-1 effort in Week 13 against Miami). The 28-year-old has yet to show he can be rel

players.name: Chiefs D/ST
players.outlook: The Chiefs have fielded a middling fantasy D/ST the past two seasons, scoring in double-digits only seven times  but finishing with zero or negative fantasy points only five times . Top draftee Mansoor Delane replaces CB Trent McDuffie, who was traded to the Rams, but the team otherwise returns largely the same starting lineup. An opening-week matchup against the Broncos should be avoided, but there are pockets of the schedule where the Chiefs would be great for streaming: Weeks 3-4 (@MIA, @LV) and Weeks 9-11 (NYJ, @ATL, ARI) especially.

players.name: David Njoku
players.outlook: Njoku signed with the Chargers after spending his first nine NFL seasons in Cleveland. The 2017 first-round pick was a late bloomer and has struggled with durability (he hasn't played a full season since 2018), but he has been a productive fantasy starter in recent years. Prior to a lost 2025 campaign, Njoku finished in the top eight among tight ends in fantasy PPG three seasons in a row. A force near the goal line, Njoku paced the position in end zone targets in both 2023 and 2024. At 30 years old, Njoku likely still has something left in the tank, but he has a tough path to fantasy relevance

players.name: Chargers D/ST
players.outlook: Chris O'Leary takes the helm as Chargers defensive coordinator, a year after this unit finished 11th in fantasy points (119). With stars like Khalil Mack, Derwin James Jr. and Tuli Tuipulotu on the roster, the Chargers should again put forth solid defensive numbers, health willing. But the biggest advantage here is the team's first-two-weeks' schedule: The Chargers host the Cardinals and Raiders, two of the most favorable D/ST matchups. Just beware that things get far tougher from there (@BUF, @SEA, DEN, @KC the next four weeks).

players.name: Ted Hurst III
players.outlook: Hurst was selected by the Buccaneers in the third round of April's draft. Granted he played at a small school, but Hurst ranked third in this rookie class target share (26%) and first in air yard share (45%) during his FBS career. A tall, vertical receiver, Hurst posted solid collegiate efficiency despite inconsistent QB play (only 68% of his 235 FBS targets were catchable, which is easily lowest among qualified WRs in this class). His 135-inch broad jump was best among wide receivers at the combine. Hurst will get some run at 'X' receiver as a rookie, but he's a longshot for consistent rookie

players.name: Fernando Mendoza
players.outlook: Mendoza was selected by the Raiders with the No. 1 overall pick in April's draft. The reigning Heisman Trophy winner and national champion, Mendoza is a big, pocket quarterback with elite accuracy (his career 7.1% off-target rate is easily the best in this rookie class) and a solid arm. Mendoza's 2025 campaign at Indiana included class-best marks in passing TDs (41) and QBR (90.3). He posted a 65-440-7 rushing line in 16 games last season and figures to add some value with his legs in the pros. Mendoza will get some run as a rookie, but his supporting cast isn't overly impressive and he may no

players.name: Chimere Dike
players.outlook: A first-team All-Pro in his first professional season, Dike broke Tim Brown's NFL rookie record for all-purpose yards. Most of that damage came as a returner (398 yards and two TDs on punts, 1,588 yards on kicks), but Dike also produced a bit as a receiver (423 yards and four TDs) and rusher (18 yards). The versatile Dike will remain a major factor in the return game, but he has added competition at wide receiver with Calvin Ridley healthy, Carnell Tate drafted fourth overall and target hog Wan'Dale Robinson signed during free agency. The 23-year-old will handle situational short-area targets

players.name: Demond Claiborne
players.outlook: Claiborne was selected by the Vikings in the sixth round of April's draft. Claiborne is an undersized back who struggled badly with efficiency during his four seasons at Wake Forest. On 558 career carries, Claiborne averaged 4.66 yards per attempt (second worst in this RB rookie class), 2.68 yards after contact and produced 5-plus yards on a class-low 32% of his carries. Also not much of a factor in the passing game, Claiborne may be limited to change-of-pace/return work in the pros. He'll open his career as a depth player behind Aaron Jones and Jordan Mason.

players.name: Samaje Perine
players.outlook: Perine is expected to resume his role as Chase Brown's primary backup in Cincinnati. The veteran back played 31% of the Bengals' snaps last season, totaling 84 carries and 21 targets. He cleared 400 total yards for the fifth consecutive season, though he has yet to reach 200 touches in a single season in his career, nor has he produced a top-30 fantasy campaign. The 30-year-old has reached double-digit fantasy points three times over the last two seasons and would require a Brown injury in order to flirt with flex appeal. He can be left on waivers.

players.name: Ollie Gordon II
players.outlook: Gordon is battling Jaylen Wright for backup work behind lead back De'Von Achane in Miami. Gordon was used sparingly as a rookie and didn't exactly move the needle. The 2025 sixth-round pick averaged an ugly 2.84 yards per carry on 70 attempts and 3.6 yards per target on the nine balls thrown his way. Gordon is still very young (22 years old), and his size (6-foot-1, 226 pounds) adds to his long-term intrigue. He'll have some insurance appeal if he beats out Wright for primary backup duties.

players.name: LeQuint Allen Jr.
players.outlook: A 2025 seventh-round pick, Allen is set to compete with fellow second-year back Bhayshul Tuten and newcomer Chris Rodriguez Jr. for work in the Jacksonville backfield. As a rookie, Allen played 22% of the Jaguars' offensive snaps (82% of which were pass plays), but was limited to just 33 touches and failed to find the end zone or reach 4.0 fantasy points in a single game. It's likely that Tuten will operate as the Jaguars' primary back, with Rodriguez busy on early downs and short-yardage situations, and Allen used as a passing-down specialist, same as in 2025. That said, none of the three are

players.name: Ty Johnson
players.outlook: Johnson has settled in as a productive change-of-pace and receiving option in the Buffalo backfield behind James Cook. Johnson enters his eighth NFL season having yet to clear 63 carries or 34 catches in a season, but his role allows for him to hit for the occasional big game (15-plus fantasy points four times over the last two seasons). Of course, those games have come at random, making Johnson an unusable fantasy commodity. Even if Cook misses time this season, it's likely that Johnson would remain in his role, with Ray Davis instead stepping into lead back duties. Johnson plays a valuable r

players.name: Colby Parkinson
players.outlook: Parkinson is set to resume his role in the Rams' TE committee. The 2020 fourth-round pick was a part-time player early last season, but graduated to a much larger role in the second half. In fact, from Week 10 on (12 games, including the playoffs), Parkinson averaged 5.0 targets and 12.1 fantasy points per game, scoring nine touchdowns along the way. He finished the regular season with career-high marks across the board, which included his first top-35 fantasy campaign (17th). If Parkinson carries his increased role into 2026, he'll be a sneaky fantasy option, but the problem is that he needs

players.name: Jordan James
players.outlook: James is an intriguing insurance stash as a candidate to work as 30-year-old Christian McCaffrey's primary backup in San Francisco. The 2025 fifth-round pick didn't record a single touch on three snaps during a rookie campaign spent buried behind McCaffrey and a host of veterans. James wasn't utilized much as a receiver at the collegiate level and underwhelmed at last year's combine, so it's unclear what his upside will be in the pros. However, if the 22-year-old wins the No. 2 gig over rookie Kaelon Black and McCaffrey misses action, he'll be a priority add. Consider him in the final few roun

players.name: Tory Horton
players.outlook: Horton had the look of a Day 3 find by Seattle early on in 2025 prior to a season-ending shin injury suffered in Week 9. The 2025 fifth-round pick opened his career buried on the depth chart behind Jaxon Smith-Njigba and Cooper Kupp, but still found a way to make an impact while being limited to 46% of the offensive snaps. Though his production was volatile and he never cleared five targets in a game, he found the end zone five times on 23 targets. Despite the impressive showing, Horton's short-term outlook is dicey with JSN, Kupp and Rashid Shaheed presumably ahead of him on the depth chart.

players.name: Tua Tagovailoa
players.outlook: Tagovailoa signed with Atlanta during the offseason after spending his first six seasons in Miami. The 2020 first-round pick showed signs of life a few years ago, which included a 4,624-yard, 29-TD season in 2023, but his production and efficiency have declined since. The final straw was a rough 2025 in which he threw 15 INTs (second most in the league) in just 14 games and was benched. Tagovailoa is a nonfactor with his legs (fewer than 75 yards in four straight seasons, with zero TDs during the span) and has, in turn, never finished better than 10th in fantasy points per game (he was 33rd in

players.name: Kaleb Johnson
players.outlook: Johnson's rookie season didn't go as planned. Drafted in the third round as a potential Najee Harris replacement, Johnson quickly found himself buried behind Jaylen Warren and Kenneth Gainwell and never recovered, even losing his kick returner role after a costly Week 2 blunder. He ended his first campaign with 78 yards on 29 touches. The 23-year-old will enter his second season with a fresh start under new coach Mike McCarthy, but he still has a steep hill to climb with Warren and newcomer Rico Dowdle ahead of him on depth chart. He's only worth rostering in dynasty.

players.name: Mason Taylor
players.outlook: Taylor was a busy man during his rookie season, playing 81% of the Jets' offensive snaps and handling a healthy 19% of the targets in 13 games. The 2025 second-round pick struggled badly with efficiency while dealing with the team's quarterback woes, ranking near the basement in catch rate (65%) and yards per target (5.4). Taylor also dropped five passes (fourth most), scored only one touchdown and finished 30th in fantasy PPG. Taylor would've been a potential 2026 breakout candidate, but that was quickly derailed when the Jets selected Kenyon Sadiq in the first round of April's draft. Taylor

players.name: Xavier Legette
players.outlook: Legette is eyeing a Year 3 leap after a boom/bust start to his NFL career. The 2024 first-round pick flashed with 521 yards and four touchdowns on 55 touches as a rookie, but fell to 363 yards and three scores on 36 touches in 2025. Legette did post a pair of big games (24.2 points in Week 7 and 18.3 points in Week 11), but was otherwise held in check (3.6 PPG in the other 13 games). Legette has struggled with the ball in his hands (woeful 2.1 RAC in his career) and is behind Tetairoa McMillan and likely Jalen Coker on the Carolina WR depth chart. The 25-year-old will see some situational targ

players.name: Elijah Sarratt
players.outlook: Sarratt was selected by the Ravens in the fourth round of April's draft. Surratt is a big, perimeter receiver who hauled in 31 touchdown receptions (most in this rookie WR class) in 40 collegiate games, which includes a FBS-high 15 in 2025. His efficiency was terrific across the board, including 10.7 yards per target, 2.69 YPRR and a 72% catch rate. Surratt is an intriguing prospect, but he may not see the field a ton as a rookie with Zay Flowers, Rashod Bateman and fellow rookie Ja'Kobi Lane also in the mix in Baltimore's low-volume pass attack. He's best as a dynasty stash.

players.name: Michael Penix Jr.
players.outlook: Penix is no longer guaranteed a starting job entering his third season. The 2024 first-round pick has appeared in 14 games and has 14 total touchdowns, a 21% off-target rate and a 60% completion percentage to show for it. Penix has done well to avoid turnovers (six career INTs), but he's a nonfactor with his legs (career 28-81-2 rushing) and failed to post a single fantasy outing better than 10th last season. Penix tore an ACL in Week 11, which further complicates his path to beating out newcomer Tua Tagovailoa for the team's Week 1 starting gig. The 26-year-old might eventually emerge into a

players.name: Seth McGowan
players.outlook: McGowan was selected by the Colts in the seventh round of April's draft. McGowan is an older prospect (25), having bounced around five schools due to an off-field issue in 2021 that led to jail time and a dismissal from Oklahoma. He slowly rebuilt his career and peaked with 1,100 yards and six TDs at New Mexico State in 2024 prior to delivering 851 yards and 12 TDs at Kentucky last season. His efficiency is hit or miss, as his career 2.65 YAC is very poor, but his 4.2 forced missed tackle rate is strong. He's been effective in the passing game, as well, so there's some hope for a pro level imp

players.name: Theo Johnson
players.outlook: Johnson was a solid find by the Giants in the fourth round of the 2024 draft, but he's headed for a reduced role this season following New York's signing of Isaiah Likely and Malik Nabers' return to health. The change comes after Johnson ranked top 12 among tight ends in both snaps and routes, but 23rd in catches and 19th in yards last season. Johnson was busy near the goal line (seven end zone targets), but struggled with drops (tight end-high nine), which led to a poor 63% catch rate. Johnson finished 23rd in fantasy PPG and now may be lucky to see a target or two per game. He's well off the

players.name: Deshaun Watson
players.outlook: Watson is expected to return to the field this season after a disastrous four years in Cleveland. A top-six fantasy QB (points per game) during each of his first four NFL seasons, Watson has appeared in a total of 19 games since joining the Browns, averaging a poor 13.1 fantasy points during the span. A torn Achilles suffered in Week 7 of 2024 (followed by tearing it again less than three months later) cost Watson all of 2025, and he'll now compete with Shedeur Sanders for Cleveland's starting job. Now 30 years old, with a young, unproven supporting cast and having not been a factor since 2020

players.name: Kirk Cousins
players.outlook: Cousins signed with the Raiders and will battle projected No. 1 overall draft selection Fernando Mendoza for the team's Week 1 starting job. Cousins made eight starts for Atlanta last season and was not much of a fantasy option, averaging 12.5 fantasy points per game while reaching 18 points only once. The 38-year-old will be a bridge starter at best until Mendoza is ready and is no longer a threat with his legs (7 yards on 14 carries last season). He won't be a fantasy option, even when on the field. He should only be drafted late in superflex leagues.

players.name: Kyle Williams
players.outlook: Williams showed some flashes as a rookie, but he has a tough path to a Year 2 breakout. The 2025 third-round pick didn't see the field much (31% snap share), but he scored three touchdowns on 21 targets, all of which came from Week 10 on. He was utilized as a situational deep threat (17.6 aDOT), which led to a low catch rate (48%) but plenty of big plays (20.9 YPR). That role may not change much in 2026, as Williams will now compete with newcomers A.J. Brown and Romeo Doubs, as well as incumbents DeMario Douglas and Mack Hollins for targets in a good New England offense led by Drake Maye. Unfo

players.name: Eli Stowers
players.outlook: Stowers was selected by the Eagles in the second round of April's draft. Stowers is a converted quarterback who improved his production each of the last three seasons, peaking with a 62-769-4 receiving line in 2025. He aligned in the slot on 72% of his collegiate routes (highest among this rookie tight end class) and his career 2.38 YPRR is easily tops in this TE class. He's not much of a blocker, but he sports good speed and athleticism (he posted the best vertical and broad jumps among TEs at the combine). Stowers will have minimal fantasy value while working behind Dallas Goedert as a rooki

players.name: Brashard Smith
players.outlook: Smith heads into his second NFL season set to compete with Emmett Johnson and Emari Demercado for No. 2 duties behind new Chiefs' lead back Kenneth Walker III. Smith played just 17% of the Chiefs' offensive snaps as a rookie and had nearly as many targets (35) as he did carries (44). The seventh-round pick wasn't overly effective (3.43 yards per carry, 4.9 yards per target) and was able to reach double-digit fantasy points only once (13.1 in a Week 7 blowout win). The undersized 23-year-old would likely share the backfield even if Walker were to miss time, and he has minimal fantasy appeal.

players.name: Shedeur Sanders
players.outlook: Sanders enters his second NFL season set to compete with Deshaun Watson for the Browns' starting quarterback gig. Sanders made eight appearances during his rookie season and wasn't overly productive, scoring eight all-purpose touchdowns, throwing 10 interceptions and completing 57% of his passes. The fifth-round pick produced one weekly fantasy finish better than 18th, though it was an impressive 364-yard passing game with four total touchdowns (33.5 points). Sanders added some value with his legs, including 20-plus yards in five straight games to end the season. The 24-year-old remains a wild

players.name: Adam Randall
players.outlook: Randall was selected by the Ravens in the fifth round of April's draft. More specifically, he was handpicked by owner Steve Bisciotti. Randall is the biggest back in this rookie class and he possesses terrific speed (4.50 40-yard dash, 113 speed score), a combination that makes him an interesting developmental flier. A converted wide receiver, Randall had a grand total of four carries during his first three seasons at Clemson prior to posting a 168-814-10 rushing line in 2025. His experience as a receiver suggests he has big upside in that area, as well (he totaled an 84-787-5 receiving line w

players.name: Hollywood Brown
players.outlook: Brown signed with the Eagles and he's likely to slot in either third or fourth on the team's depth chart behind DeVonta Smith, first-round rookie Makai Lemon and perhaps Dontayvion Wicks. Once a featured target in Baltimore and Arizona, Brown was more of a situational player during his two seasons in Kansas City. He barely saw the field in 2024 due to injury before handling a career-low 14.2% target share in 16 games in 2025. Brown cleared 10 fantasy points three times, but all came prior to Week 7. With Dallas Goedert and Saquon Barkley also heavily in the mix for targets in Philly, Brown wil

players.name: Mike Gesicki
players.outlook: There was an era when Gesicki was a viable starting option in fantasy, but that time has come and gone. Since posting back-to-back top-eight fantasy campaigns in 2020 and 2021, Gesicki has finished 23rd, 37th, 13th and 41st the past four seasons. The latter came during a 2025 campaign in which he was limited to 41 targets in 13 games. Gesicki is no more than a situational seam stretcher and not much of an option near the goal line (he has exactly two TDs and five end zone targets each of the past three seasons). The 30-year-old will be a risky streaming option even if Ja'Marr Chase or Tee Higg

players.name: Skyler Bell
players.outlook: Bell was selected by the Bills in the fourth round of April's draft. Bell is an undersized, but versatile, receiver who finished 2025 second in the nation (first in this WR rookie class) in receiving yards (1,278) and, while he had a class-high 25 drops across 52 collegiate games, he was better in this area last season (five drops on 146 targets). Bell showed well at the combine, running a solid 4.40 40-yard dash and posting terrific marks in the vertical and broad jump. With DJ Moore and Khalil Shakir locked in atop Buffalo's WR depth chart, Bell will compete with Keon Coleman and Josh Palmer

players.name: Trey Benson
players.outlook: Benson's pro career is off to a slow start due primarily to a variety of injuries. The 2024 third-round pick was essentially splitting the Arizona backfield with James Conner last season, but he was never able to return to the field after suffering a knee injury in Week 4. He was effective prior to the injury, averaging 5.5 yards per carry, and was busy as a receiver (four-plus targets in three straight games). The 24-year-old heads into 2026 no longer assured of a role with a new coaching staff and after the team added Jeremiyah Love and Tyler Allgeier to a running back room that still includ

players.name: Jake Tonges
players.outlook: Tonges enters his fourth NFL season very much on the fantasy radar due to a torn Achilles suffered by George Kittle during last season's playoffs. Kittle is expected to return at some point this season, but while he's out, Tonges is set to replace him as the 49ers' top pass catcher at the position. Kittle missed seven full games last season, including the playoffs (Weeks 2-6, 17, 20). During those games, Tonges handled a 17.9% target share (6.6 per game) and posted a 34-328-3 receiving line. That works out to 11.8 fantasy PPG, which would've ranked eighth among all tight ends last season, ahea

players.name: Darnell Washington
players.outlook: Though he never quite made it onto the fantasy radar, Washington was one of the most fun, surprising "breakout" players of 2025. Essentially an extension of the offensive line at 6-foot-6, 264 pounds, Washington is known mainly for his blocking. Still, the 2023 third-round pick played well enough that he was stealing snaps and targets from both Jonnu Smith and Pat Freiermuth. Washington never cleared six targets or 10.7 fantasy points in any game, but he was effective with the ball in his hands and averaged 8.5 yards per target. Though Smith has been released, Pittsburgh's offense is no longer

players.name: Michael Mayer
players.outlook: Mayer enters his first contract year expected to resume his role as Las Vegas' oft-utilized No. 2 TE behind Brock Bowers. The 2023 second-round pick has yet to come close to playing a full season, nor has he emerged as a reliable fantasy option. Last season, he averaged 2.9 targets and 3.4 fantasy points in nine games with Bowers, compared to 6.0 targets and 10.9 PPG in the four games in which Bowers was sidelined. A short-range target (career 5.5 aDOT) with minimal goal line work (one career end zone target), Mayer is way off the fantasy radar. He should be added to rosters only if Bowers mis

players.name: Oscar Delp
players.outlook: Delp was selected by the Saints in the third round of April's draft. Delp was busy during his final three seasons at Georgia (1,733 snaps in 42 games), but that didn't lead to much work in the passing game (no more than 24 catches, 284 yards or a 7% target share in a single season). Good speed and hands suggest there's some hope for him as a developmental piece, which is what he'll be in 2026 while playing a situational role behind Juwan Johnson and Noah Fant.

players.name: Elijah Arroyo
players.outlook: Arroyo is eyeing a Year 2 breakout after an underwhelming rookie campaign in which he played a clear second fiddle to A.J. Barner. The 2025 second-round pick was limited to 39% of the offensive snaps during the 13 games he was active. He cleared three targets in a game only once (five in Week 7) and his lone touchdown came on one of just two targets in Week 9. Arroyo was effective as a vertical target at the collegiate level, so he remains an intriguing dynasty hold, but the 23-year-old has a tough path to short-term fantasy relevance while stuck behind Barner in Seattle's low-pass-volume offe

players.name: Bryce Lance
players.outlook: Lance was selected by the Saints in the fourth round of April's draft. Trey's little brother is the lone wide receiver in this rookie class who didn't play a single snap at the FBS level. However, he was productive as a perimeter receiver at North Dakota State, posting receiving lines of 75-1,053-17 and 51-1,079-8 over the last two seasons. He's a year or so older than most of his classmates, but he dominated at the combine with terrific showings in the 40-yard dash (4.34), vertical (41.5) and broad jump (133). He has the size and skillset to battle Devaughn Vele for New Orleans' No. 3 gig beh

players.name: Jalen Tolbert
players.outlook: Tolbert signed with Miami after spending his first four NFL seasons in Dallas. The 2022 third-round pick has a path to a substantial offensive role, with Malik Washington, Tutu Atwell and rookies Chris Bell and Caleb Douglas as his top competition for snaps and targets. We have seen Tolbert as a near-full-time player in a much better offense and he wasn't much of a fantasy option. That came in 2024 when he played 76% of the Cowboys' offensive snaps. He found the end zone seven times, but was held to 610 yards and finished 54th among receivers in fantasy PPG. Tolbert played a reduced role last

players.name: Carson Beck
players.outlook: Beck was selected by the Cardinals in the third round of April's draft. Beck is a big, experienced quarterback who started for two seasons at Georgia prior to leading Miami to the national championship game last season. Beck paced this rookie QB class in completion percentage last season (72.4%) and for his career (69.5%), while also leading this group with an 80.9 QBR and 8.4 YPA during his 55-game collegiate career. He's unlikely to offer much with his legs in the pros, however, and will begin his career behind Jacoby Brissett and likely Gardner Minshew. Beck has no short-term fantasy value,

players.name: Eli Raridon
players.outlook: Raridon was selected by the Patriots in the third round of April's draft. Raridon is a tall, blocking tight end who was barely targeted (5% share) and totaled a 48-623-3 receiving line during four seasons at Notre Dame. Most of the receiving work came in 2025, so perhaps there's some hope in that area, but he's a long shot for fantasy value any time soon, especially with Hunter Henry and likely Julian Hill ahead of him on the depth chart this season.

players.name: Buccaneers D/ST
players.outlook: A middling, matchups-driven D/ST last season, the Buccaneers saw much change among their linebacker corps during the offseason. Lavonte David retired, and the team drafted Rueben Bain Jr. 15th overall and signed Alex Anzalone and Christian Rozeboom. Take a wait-and-see approach to how the new personnel jells, especially since the Buccaneers get a tough opening matchup in a road game against the Bengals.

players.name: Tyler Higbee
players.outlook: Higbee re-signed with the Rams and will battle for work with the likes of Colby Parkinson, Davis Allen, Terrance Ferguson and rookie Max Klare. The 2016 fourth-round pick has a pair of top-10 fantasy campaigns in his career, but the last one came in 2022 and he's finished 24th or worse in three consecutive seasons. Injuries have been part of the issue (21 missed games over the last two seasons), but so has a lesser role and minimal goal-line work (seven touchdowns and four end zone targets over the last three years). Now 33 years old, Higbee is likely third in line for targets at his position

players.name: Packers D/ST
players.outlook: Micah Parsons' health has a bearing on the performance of this defense; it was 13th in fantasy points across the 13 games before his ACL tear, but had a negative score in four games without him. Tuck that away before diving head first into the team's soft September schedule (@MIN, @NYJ, ATL the first three weeks), though those are matchups that make this defense well worth streaming consideration.

players.name: J.J. McCarthy
players.outlook: McCarthy's career is off to a slow start after the 2024 first-round pick missed his entire rookie season because of an injury then struggled through 2025. McCarthy appeared in 10 games and totaled 11 passing TDs and 12 interceptions while completing an ugly 58% of his passes. McCarthy added some value with his legs (including four TDs), but his production was extremely inconsistent (18-plus fantasy points in four games, but 6.7 per game in his other six outings). The 23-year-old still has plenty of time to develop, but that will come as a backup to Kyler Murray this season. McCarthy is worth c

players.name: Dawson Knox
players.outlook: Knox enters his eighth season as a solid role player for the Buffalo offense. He is on the field quite a bit (20th among tight ends in snaps last season), but defers to Dalton Kincaid when it comes to the team's top target priority at the TE position. Even when Kincaid was sidelined last season, Knox was limited to only 3.6 targets and 6.1 fantasy points per game. Knox has never posted a top-10 fantasy campaign and has finished outside the top 30 in PPG each of the last three seasons. Even if Kincaid misses additional time, Knox will max out as a fantasy TE2.

players.name: Mac Jones
players.outlook: Jones returns for his second go as Brock Purdy's backup in San Francisco after showing well in relief duties in eight starts last season. In those eight appearances, Jones completed 70% of his passes and threw 13 touchdowns to six interceptions. The 2021 first-round pick was a nonfactor with his legs (28-64-0), however, which limited him to an underwhelming 16.3 fantasy PPG. Should Purdy miss time in 2026, Jones will be no more than a fringe QB2. The 28-year-old shouldn't be considered on draft day.

players.name: Max Klare
players.outlook: Klare was selected by the Rams in the second round of April's draft. Klare is a receiving tight end who has experience playing in line and in the slot. He might not offer much as a blocker in the pros, but he showed his receiving ability at two different schools, posting a 51-685-4 line with Purdue in 2024 and a 43-448-2 line with Ohio State in 2025. Klare has the speed and athleticism to eventually emerge as a fantasy option, but hell begin his career in a crowded tight end room that also includes Colby Parkinson, Tyler Higbee, Davis Allen and 2025 second-round pick Terrance Ferguson. Klare i

players.name: Brenen Thompson
players.outlook: Thompson was selected by the Chargers in the fourth round of April's draft. Thompson is an extremely small and very fast (4.26 40-yard dash) receiver who posted a rookie-class-high 18.5 YPR during his career and handled a massive 43% of Mississippi State's air yards last season. He didn't see much work prior to 2025, however, and figures to operate as a situational deep threat in the pros. He'll battle second-years Tre Harris and KeAndre Lamber-Smith for occasional looks behind Ladd McConkey and Quentin Johnston this season.

players.name: Ja'Tavion Sanders
players.outlook: Sanders is back as a pass-catching tight end in Carolina, though he's unlikely to see a larger share of the target pie with veteran Darren Waller now in the mix. Sanders - a 2024 fourth-round pick - flashed as a rookie with a 33-342-1 receiving line while playing 55% of Carolina's offensive snaps and handling 9.1% of the targets across 16 games. He simply didn't progress in Year 2, posting a 29-190-1 line while playing 52% of the snaps and handling a 10% target share in 12 healthy games. Sanders has been an inefficient short-range target with little goal line activity thus far (four career end

players.name: Jaguars D/ST
players.outlook: Anthony Campanile's defense was one of the most surprisingly productive of 2025, finishing fifth in fantasy points, and the team was fortunate to get him back for this year. That said, the team had modest sack and fumble recovery numbers, and it did lose LB Devin Lloyd and CB Greg Newsome over the offseason. Fantasy managers can still freely select this defense, knowing it has one of the best opening-week matchups by hosting the Browns, but they'll likely need to swap them out for Weeks 2 through 6 (@DEN, NE, @CIN, PHI, HOU).

players.name: Saints D/ST
players.outlook: While the Saints showed improvement under first-year defensive coordinator Brandon Staley over the course of 2025 -- their 66 fantasy points following their Week 11 bye was fifth-best in the league -- the team has a rough go of it at the onset of 2026. Road matchups with the Lions (Week 1) and Ravens (2) are tough as nails, and even the addition of LB Kaden Ellis isn't going to ease those matchup worries. Consider this a streaming defense at best.

players.name: Malik Benson
players.outlook: Benson was selected by the Raiders in the sixth round of April's draft. An accomplished sprinter, the speedy Benson has big play written all over him, though he's a slightly older prospect and his collegiate production was limited by a lot of changes in scenery (two years of community college followed by 2023 at Alabama, 2024 at Florida State and 2025 at Oregon). Benson never cleared a 15% target share in a single season, peaking with a 43-719-6 receiving line in 2025. Benson is a longshot as a sixth rounder, but the Raiders' shaky wide receiver depth chart presents him with an opportunity to

players.name: Justin Fields
players.outlook: After failing to lock down a starting gig with the Bears, Steelers and Jets, Fields was traded to the Chiefs and will move forward as Patrick Mahomes' backup. That's obviously unlikely to lead to much playing time, but with Mahomes recovering from a torn ACL, there's a small chance Fields could get some early-season run in 2026. Should Fields start, he'll find his way into the QB1 discussion because of his elite rushing ability (45.1 rush rushing yards per game last season and four-plus rushing TDs in four straight seasons). In seven full games last season, Fields averaged 19.2 fantasy points,

players.name: Eli Heidenreich
players.outlook: Heidenreich was selected by the Steelers in the seventh round of April's draft. Heidenreich is an intriguing prospect, as he's a tweener who could play running back or receiver in the pros. The Navy product never cleared 77 carries in a single season, but did post a 51-941-6 receiving line in 2025. For his career, he averaged 6.85 yards per carry and evaded one tackle for every 5.9 touches, both of which are best in this RB rookie class. If he makes the Steelers' roster he'll likely max out as a gadget player behind Jaylen Warren and Rico Dowdle.

players.name: Ty Simpson
players.outlook: Simpson was selected by the Rams in the first round of April's draft. Simpson was a one-year starter at Alabama and wasn't overly impressive statistically, completing 64% of his passes and posting a pedestrian 76.6 QBR. He's fairly accurate with an average arm, but he's a bit undersized and doesn't figure to move the needle a ton with his legs (62-309-2 rushing in 2025). Simpson won't see the field consistently until Matthew Stafford retires, so he's well off the 2026 fantasy radar. Keep him stashed in dynasty, especially superflex formats.

players.name: Savion Williams
players.outlook: Williams is primed for a larger role in his second NFL season. The 2025 third-round pick had a unique rookie campaign, handling more carries (11) than he did targets (10). Williams' gadget role allowed him only 90 snaps (12%) and he was utilized only near the line of scrimmage (1.4 aDOT). The Green Bay WR rotation no longer includes Romeo Doubs or Dontayvion Wicks, but Christian Watson, Jayden Reed and fellow second-year wideout Matthew Golden remain in the mix. Williams will need to beat out one (or perhaps two) of them and start to see more downfield targets in order to land on the fantasy r

players.name: Kevin Coleman Jr.
players.outlook: Coleman Jr. was selected by the Dolphins in the fifth round of April's draft. Coleman is a small, slot receiver and punt returner who aligned inside on 83% of his 943 collegiate pass routes. Despite playing at three different FBS schools over the last three seasons, Coleman handled a solid 21% target share during the span and played well, catching 72% of his targets and dropping only four of 229 targets (1.7%). He posted a weak, 88 speed score at the combine, running a 4.49 40-yard dash at 179 pounds. Coleman will battle fellow rookies Chris Bell and Caleb Douglas, as well as a host of veteran

players.name: Anthony Richardson Sr.
players.outlook: Richardson enters his fourth NFL season currently as a backup to Daniel Jones, but still a candidate to be traded. Last season, Richardson played just 14 snaps off the bench and missed most of the season with an eye injury. If ever called on to start, Richardson will be an interesting fantasy wild card. On one hand, the 2023 fourth-overall pick has a ton of upside; he ranked no lower than sixth among QBs in carries, rushing yards and rush TDs in 2024 despite only playing 10 full games, while also pacing the position in average depth of throw and yards per completion. That led to four 20-plus f

players.name: Zavion Thomas
players.outlook: Thomas was selected by the Bears in the third round of April's draft. The LSU product is small (5'10/190), but extremely fast (4.28 40-yard dash) and figures to make his hay as a situational rusher, receiver and returner in the pros. He was limited to a 13% target share across his final three collegiate seasons (one at Mississippi State and two at LSU), having failed to clear 41 catches, 536 receiving yards or five touchdowns in any of the three campaigns. He'll battle Kalif Raymond and Jahdae Walker for work behind Rome Odunze and Luther Burden III. Thomas is unlikely to emerge into a reliabl

players.name: Jameis Winston
players.outlook: Winston is back with the Giants and with Russell Wilson out of the picture, he is expected to serve as the primary backup to Jaxson Dart in 2026. Winston hasn't been a full-time starter since 2019 and was limited to two starts last season. In typical Winston style, results varied, with 11.0 fantasy points against Green Bay in Week 11, followed by a 32.2-point showing against Detroit the very next week. The 32-year-old doesn't do much with his legs, but his boom/bust passing style makes him an occasional streaming option when the matchup is right. That's what he'll be, if called on for a spot s

players.name: Joe Flacco
players.outlook: Flacco re-signed with the Bengals and will back up Joe Burrow this season. The veteran quarterback made six starts for Cincinnati last season and showed well, totaling 14 touchdowns and four interceptions while averaging 19.9 fantasy PPG. The 41-year-old can still sling it, but he's a nonfactor with his legs and hasn't finished a season better than 20th in fantasy points since 2014. If Burrow is sidelined, Flacco will do enough through the air to land in the QB2 discussion, but that's his ceiling.

players.name: Jets D/ST
players.outlook: The first team to make it through a season without recording an interception since the category began being tracked in 1933, the Jets finished last in defensive fantasy scoring last season. Hey, they can only go up from here, right? Perhaps, but offseason additions of LB Demario Davis, S Minkah Fitzpatrick and LB David Bailey (the No. 2 overall pick in the draft) hardly vault this unit into the position's upper echelon. They do get a great matchup against the Titans in Week 1, though, so there's that?

players.name: 49ers D/ST
players.outlook: Raheem Morris comes aboard as the 49ers' defensive coordinator this season, and between questions about his scheme's fit to the team's personnel and the injuries that have struck this roster in recent years, it's tough to get fully behind a rebound from this D/ST. An opening-week road matchup with the Rams should make this a no-go draft day pick, but the 49ers could have their matchup moments later in the year.

players.name: Barion Brown
players.outlook: Brown was selected by the Saints in the sixth round of April's draft. Brown is a thin, vertical receiver who handled a healthy 21% target share across 50 collegiate games at Kentucky and LSU. Brown struggled a bit with drops and efficiency, but made some noise as a rusher (32-228-2 across four seasons) and figures to make his biggest impact as a kick returner (65 kick returns for 1,910 yards and six TDs are all easily tops in this rookie class). With Chris Olave and Jordyn Tyson cemented atop the depth chart, Brown is well off the fantasy radar.

players.name: Jam Miller
players.outlook: Miller was selected by the Patriots in the seventh round of April's draft. Miller has decent size, but he has struggled with effectiveness, posting a 4.57 YPC (worst in this rookie class) during his collegiate career (including an ugly 3.88 in 2025). Poor tackle breaking and YAC numbers give him perhaps the worst efficiency profile in this RB class, and he hasn't shown much in the passing game (career 40-336-2 line). He ran a solid 4.42 40-yard dash at the combine but posted the worst marks in this RB class in the vertical and broad jump. He'll be buried on the New England depth chart if he ma

players.name: Oronde Gadsden
players.outlook: Gadsden's rookie season was quite the roller coaster. The 2025 fifth-round pick didn't get much early run prior to exploding for 29.4 fantasy points in Week 7 and 18.7 points in Week 8. He went on to score one touchdown and average 6.2 fantasy PPG the rest of the season, never clearing 12.2 points in a single outing. Gadsden finished the season eighth or better at the position in end zone targets, aDOT, YPR, YPT and YPRR. The 23-year-old's second-half fall is concerning, and he now enters Year 2 set to compete for work with newcomer David Njoku. It's still possible Gadsden emerges as a feature

players.name: Cowboys D/ST
players.outlook: The Cowboys underwent a major roster overhaul and finished on a massive cold spell defensively late last season, making it difficult to get behind them as a fantasy option at the onset of 2026. Only the Jets scored fewer fantasy points for the year. The Cowboys did restock their roster during the offseason, adding Caleb Downs, Jalen Thompson and Rashan Gary (among others), and they do have a Giants matchup to open their schedule. It's still better to wait and see how this unit jells before diving in, however, even from a streaming standpoint.

players.name: Colts D/ST
players.outlook: So much is stacked against the Colts' defense at the onset of 2026. They were the second-worst scorer over the second half of 2025, in large part due to injuries to key performers, they lost CB Kenny Moore and LB Zaire Franklin during the offseason, and they have one of the most brutal opening schedules of any team (BAL, @KC, HOU the first three weeks). This is more of a wait-and-see D/ST than one to target on draft day.

players.name: Vikings D/ST
players.outlook: Brian Flores' blitz-happy defense has managed exactly 49 sacks, fourth-most in the league, in each of the past two seasons, playing a big part in the team finishing among the position's top seven in fantasy scoring in each of those years. Though Jonathan Allen and Jonathan Greenard are no longer with the team, the Vikings' draft selections of DTs Caleb Banks and Domonique Orange should at least keep them competitive up front. That said, the Vikings face a brutal opening schedule (GB, Week 1; @CHI, Week 2) and have one of the toughest second-half schedules in the league. Be prepared to pivot if

players.name: Bengals D/ST
players.outlook: Only three defenses scored fewer fantasy points than did the Bengals last season, and other than adding DT Dexter Lawrence, the team did little to upgrade the unit during the offseason. That said, few teams have as favorable a D/ST schedule than do the Bengals, so with some early promise, they could be a streaming option for matchups against the Dolphins (Week 5), Titans (8), Saints (12), Browns (13 and 18) and Panthers (15).

players.name: Cade Klubnik
players.outlook: Klubnik was selected by the Jets in the fourth round of April's draft. Klubnik is an undersized, conservative quarterback who ranked last in this rookie class in aDOT (7.4), yards per completion (11.1), yards per attempt (7.1) and QB rating (136) during his collegiate tenure. He peaked with a 36-to-6 TD-to-INT showing in 2024, but fell to 16 TDs and six INTs in 2025. Klubnik does have a lot of experience (three years as a starter at Clemson) and could add value with his legs (totaled a 294-1,429-17 rushing line in his career), though he was extremely inefficient in the latter in 2025. Klubnik

players.name: Marlin Klein
players.outlook: Klein was selected by the Texans in the second round of April's draft. He's an inexperienced, blocking tight end who posted an ugly 5.5 YPT and 57.6% catch rate in his collegiate career. Klein peaked with a 24-248-1 receiving line in 2025 and now joins a Texans' offense that already includes Dalton Schultz, Cade Stover and Foster Moreau at the tight end position. Klein may be Houston's tight end of the future, but he won't be on the fantasy radar as a rookie.

players.name: Riley Leonard
players.outlook: Leonard is expected to operate as the Colts' No. 2 quarterback this season. It's a notable designation, as starter Daniel Jones continues to recover from a torn Achilles suffered in Week 14 last season. Should Jones miss time to begin the 2026 season, Leonard is positioned to start. Leonard made one start as a rookie, throwing for 270 yards and two touchdowns and rushing for 21 yards and an additional score, primarily against Houston's backup defense in Week 18. The 2025 sixth-round pick adds value with his legs, but he'd be no more than a fringe QB2 even if called on to start.

players.name: Riley Nowakowski
players.outlook: Nowakowski was selected by the Steelers in the fifth round of April's draft. Nowakowski is a bit undersized with very small hands, but he's a capable blocker and, after totaling 18 catches in 36 games at Wisconsin, made a little bit of a leap as a pass catcher in 2025 (his lone season at Indiana), posting a 32-387-2 receiving line. He's expected to play fullback and offer some tight end depth behind Pat Freiermuth and Darnell Washington.

players.name: Will Kacmarek
players.outlook: Kacmarek was selected by the Dolphins in the third round of April's draft. Kacmarek is a massive, strong blocking tight end who won't see much receiving work in the pros. He's likely to play a lot of snap as a rookie considering Miami's shaky roster, but Greg Dulcich is expected to operate as the team's top pass-catcher at the tight end position. Kacmarek is no more than the deepest of deep sleepers.

players.name: Tanner Koziol
players.outlook: Koziol was selected by the Jaguars in the fifth round of April's draft. Across 49 collegiate games at Houston and Ball State, Koziol produced 349 targets, 237 receptions, 2,234 yards, 24 TDs, a 23% target share and a 24% air yard share. All six stats easily top this TE rookie class and that production included a massive 94-839-8 showing in 2024. Koziol has work to do as a blocker, but his size and production suggest there's clear receiving upside. He's worth stashing in dynasty, but doesn't have a path to short-term value behind Brenton Strange and likely fellow rookie Nick Boerkircher.

players.name: Sam Roush
players.outlook: Roush was selected by the Bears in the third round of April's draft. Roush is a huge, in-line blocking tight end. Though he did catch 40-plus passes each of his final two seasons at Stanford (including a healthy 22% target share in 2025), his overall receiving efficiency was underwhelming (6.6 YPT, 1.22 YPRR) and he totaled four TDs on 182 career targets. He's unlikely to see enough target volume in the pros to find his way to the fantasy radar and that's especially the case in Chicago, as he's buried behind Colston Loveland and Cole Kmet.

players.name: Reggie Virgil
players.outlook: Virgil was selected by the Cardinals in the fifth round of April's draft. Virgil is a tall, thin, perimeter, vertical receiver who ranked near the top of this WR rookie class in aDOT (14.7) and YPR (15.8) but near the basement in RAC (4.5), catch rate (54%) and YPRR (1.79) during his career at Miami Ohio and Texas Tech. A class-high 48% of his targets came on deep routes, though he played a more well-rounded role in 2025 -- his lone season with the Red Raiders. Virgil ran a 4.57 40-yard dash at 187 pounds at the combine, which works out to a poor speed score of 86. Virgil will battle Kendrick

players.name: Josh Cameron
players.outlook: Cameron was selected by the Jaguars in the sixth round of April's draft. Cameron is a big, strong, perimeter receiver who aligned out wide on 84% of his collegiate routes across five seasons at Baylor. Cameron's overall efficiency is underwhelming (1.58 YPRR), but he was certainly busy the last two seasons, totaling 52-754-10 and 69-872-9 receiving lines. He'll begin his career no higher than fifth on the Jacksonville depth chart behind Brian Thomas Jr., Jakobi Meyers, Parker Washington and Travis Hunter.

players.name: Nate Boerkircher
players.outlook: Boerkircher was selected by the Jaguars in the second round of April's draft. Boerkircher is a blocking tight end who handled a 3% target share (lowest in this rookie TE class) across 52 collegiate games (five seasons). He aligned in the slot 30% of the time and posted a 1.04 YPRR, both of which are lowest in this TE group. He'll file in as a blocking complement to starter Brenton Strange and is not a fantasy option.

players.name: Giants D/ST
players.outlook: The Giants' linebacker corps is their D/ST strength, and it's possible this could be a sneaky-good source of sacks. Nevertheless, it's almost impossible to make a case to draft them, being that they face the Cowboys and Rams to open 2026. Should the Giants impress in those games, however, they could be a prime pickup for a soft Weeks 3-6 portion of their schedule (TEN, ARI, @WSH, NO).

players.name: Bears D/ST
players.outlook: Despite leading the league in turnovers generated (33), the Bears' defense finished a middling 16th in fantasy points last season. The team subsequently replaced Jaquan Brisker, Kevin Byard and Tremaine Edmunds with Devin Bush, Coby Bryant and Dillon Thieneman during the offseason, meaning this will probably again be a matchups-oriented unit. Consider the Bears for favorable early matchups against the Panthers (Week 1) and Jets (4).

players.name: Titans D/ST
players.outlook: The Titans finished 25th in fantasy scoring from the D/ST last season, and other than draftees Dl Keldrick Faulk and LB Anthony Hill, didn't do much to substantially upgrade during the offseason. This looks like a one-and-done streamer, as the Titans face the Jets at home, a plus matchup, but are then a no-go in fantasy for the month that follows (PHI, @NYG, @BAL, HOU, @IND).

players.name: Panthers D/ST
players.outlook: Ejiro Evero coaxed a No. 15 positional finish in terms of fantasy points from this defense last season, and the defensive front has been fortified since with the additions of Devin Lloyd and Jaelen Phillips. There should be streaming potential with this D/ST, which could be worth the pickup for matchups in Weeks 3 (@CLE), 10 (@NO), 14 (NO) and 16 (@PIT).

players.name: Commanders D/ST
players.outlook: After a miserable 2025 that saw them surrender the most yards while scoring the third-fewest fantasy points, the Commanders brought in a slew of offseason reinforcements, though it was more of a quantitative than qualitative process. There's no reason to trust this D/ST in Weeks 1 and 2, which are road matchups with the Eagles and Cowboys, but if the Commanders show midseason promise, bear in mind its most favorable matchups come during the season's second half.

players.name: Falcons D/ST
players.outlook: Jeff Ulbrich's blitz-happy defense fueled 57 sacks, the league's second-best total, and a 13th best ranking in fantasy points. That approach could make this a streaming-worthy unit against weaker opposing quarterbacks, which could be the case with the Panthers (Weeks 2 and 18), Saints (4 and 17) and Browns (13). For those in deeper leagues, this could be an advantageous matchups-driven September D/ST if you wait until the end of the draft to fill the position.

players.name: Bills D/ST
players.outlook: Run defense was the Bills' undoing last season, as they allowed a league-worst 24 rushing scores and snapped a seven-year streak of placing among the position's top 10 in fantasy points scored. Jim Leonhard was brought in as defensive coordinator, switching from a 4-3 to 3-4 scheme, though the team's personnel remains light up front. Regard the Bills a D/ST streaming candidate, and one better to leave undrafted due to their rough early schedule (@HOU, DET, LAC, NE, @LAR).

players.name: Raiders D/ST
players.outlook: The Raiders have a lengthy track record of defensive struggles, finishing in the upper half of the league in fantasy points from the D/ST in only one of the past 15 seasons. Still, the team added LBs Nakobe Dean and Quay Walker and CB Taron Johnson during the offseason, and it does still have DE Maxx Crosby on board. There could be some streaming potential here in favorable Weeks 1 (MIA) and 3 (@NO) matchups.

players.name: Cardinals D/ST
players.outlook: The seeds are here for the Cardinals to have a respectable pass defense -- Budda Baker, Josh Sweat and Will Johnson all return -- but a lot would need to go right for Nick Rallis' defense to become a fantasy force. As is, the Cardinals have one of the league's toughest D/ST schedules, largely due to their playing in last year's winningest division -- their three division rivals combined to go 38-13. But hey, they do have what could be a great fantasy-playoff schedule (NYJ, @NO, LV, from Weeks 15-17), if they show us anything early.

players.name: Dolphins D/ST
players.outlook: The rebuilding Dolphins are woefully lacking in talent on both sides of the football, and they're coming off a season in which they tied for 21st in fantasy points from the D/ST. An opening-week matchup against the Raiders could make them a viable streaming choice -- though that's directed more at you 12-, 14-team and Knockout managers ? but there's little else to like here, especially with one of the toughest overall schedules in the league ahead.

players.name: Drew Allar
players.outlook: Allar was selected by the Steelers in the third round of April's draft. Allar is one of the biggest quarterbacks in this rookie class and, while he has the arm to go with his frame, accuracy is a big concern. Allar was conservative during his time at Penn State (7.6 aDOT), but he still completed only 63% of his passes and averaged 7.4 yards per attempt. In 2025, he had the worst QBR in this rookie class prior to suffering a season-ending broken ankle. On the plus side, he could add value with his legs, as he posted a career 181-1,030-12 rushing line and his 8.3% scramble rate is second highest

players.name: Josh Cuevas
players.outlook: Cuevas was selected by the Ravens in the fifth round of April's draft. Cuevas wasn't targeted much during three collegiate seasons at Washington and Alabama (57-793-6, 5% target share), but he was effective when called on, averaging 10.4 yards per target. He's a bit of a tweener and underwhelmed athletically at the combine, but can help as a blocker and receiver. He'll battle fellow rookie Matthew Hibner for snaps behind Mark Andrews and Durham Smythe this season.
